## Goal
A phone-only removal (BL-IN-08) lives or dies on comparing the person's number with what a page shows. `digits()` (`engine/matcher.py:99-101`) removes every non-digit and keeps the last 10 digits, which handles "+1" and punctuation, but a page showing "(217) 555-0142 ext. 5" or "217-555-0142 x12" becomes `5550142012`-style garbage (the extension digits push the number out of the last-10 window), so `score` and `score_value` (`matcher.py:207-258`, `278-290`) see no match for the person's own number. Cut the number at an extension marker (`x`, `ext`, `ext.`, `extension`, `#`, case-insensitive) before extracting digits, keeping the rest of `digits` unchanged. A masked number ("(217) ***-0142") must still never count as an exact match.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Table: "(217) 555-0142", "217.555.0142", "+1 217 555 0142", "1-217-555-0142", "217 555 0142 ext. 5", "217-555-0142 x12", "217-555-0142 #4", "217-555-0142 Extension 12" all give `2175550142`.
2. Inputs with fewer than 10 digits are returned as their digits, as today (no padding); `None` and empty return "".
3. A masked number ("(217) ***-0142", "217-XXX-0142") never equals the full number and never produces the `phone` signal in `score` for a candidate whose only phone is masked (assert the reasons list).
4. For a profile with the phone "217-555-0142" and a lookup page that shows "(217) 555-0142 x9", `score_value(profile, c, "phone")` returns POSSIBLE with reason `phone_lookup` (not NO_MATCH), and for a different number returns NO_MATCH.
5. `digits` of a number followed by an unrelated long digit string in the same text ("call 217-555-0142 or order 998877665544") is unchanged from today (document: the function takes one number, callers pass one value; assert today's behaviour so a change is deliberate).
6. WO-257/276/277 tests, the existing matcher tests and the reply-matcher fuzz test pass unchanged.
